Six new picture sets, each with its own line drawing (Picture words): a shopping street (13 words: bakery, greengrocer, fish shop, butcher, florist, bookshop, shoe shop, barber's, supermarket, till, bag, shop assistant, vending machine), the pharmacy counter (16 words: pharmacist, prescription, medicine bag, medicine notebook, tablet, capsule, powder, syrup, eye drops, ointment, compress and more; kinds of medicine only, no names or doses), kitchen tools (14), a bed space on the ward (14: curtain, pillow, sheet, blanket, nurse call button, over-bed table, drawer, locker and more), sports and hobbies (16) and the clock and calendar (14: yesterday, today, tomorrow, last week, this week, next week, weekend, public holiday and more). 87 new words and 60 new Listen and point sentences; Picture words now has 44 sets, 592 words and 29 drawings. Every set has Learn, Identify, Label it, Listen and point and a print sheet.

Picture mode in the Vocabulary quiz: choose any deck, then Picture. You see a picture (an emoji card, or a drawing with one pin marked) and choose the Japanese word; the other choices come from the same picture when possible. After each answer you can listen, open the word page or open the picture. Best scores are kept per deck like the other modes, misses go to My mistakes, and the Progress page lists the mode.

Two drawings redrawn: the arm and hand is now a whole arm from the shoulder with a bent elbow, a wrist and an open hand with five separate fingers and nails; the kitchen stove now has two visible burners with the pot and the frying pan on them and an oven door below. The words and sentences of both sets are unchanged.
All Japanese is a draft until a native Japanese-speaking clinician reviews it. Each new set was written and drawn by one writer and checked by a separate reviewer.
